note:
**The meaning of the two verses**
﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا أَتَوْا عَلَىٰ وَادِ النَّمْلِ قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَسَاكِنَكُمْ لَا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمَانُ وَجُنُودُهُ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾
﴿فَتَبَسَّمَ ضَاحِكًا مِّن قَوْلِهَا وَقَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَالِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَالِحًا تَرْضَاهُ وَأَدْخِلْنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِي عِبَادِكَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾
Until, when they reached the Valley of the Ants, an ant said: "O ants, enter your dwellings, so that Sulayman and his armies do not destroy you while they do not know it." So he smiled, laughing at what this ant said, because of her understanding and how she was guided to warn the ants. He felt Allah's blessing upon him, and turned to Him in du'a: "My Lord, inspire me and enable me to thank You for Your blessing which You have bestowed on me and on my parents, and to do righteous deeds that You are pleased with from me; and admit me by Your mercy into the bliss of Your Paradise among Your righteous servants, whose deeds You are pleased with."

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did the ant do when she felt the army coming? And why did she not run away alone?
2. The ant said: ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ (while they do not know it). What does that teach us when someone hurts us without meaning to?
3. Sulayman (peace be upon him) was a prophet and a great king, so what did he do when he heard what she said? (He smiled, then thanked his Lord for His blessing and made du'a to Him, and he was not arrogant.)

**This week's exercise**
This week your child is "the ant of the house": they alert the family to what benefits them, like switching off a light, closing a door or reminding someone of an appointment. And if someone wrongs them without meaning to, they say, "He didn't mean it," and tell you about it in the evening.
